headline: 8.34%: Inflation rises again in September after fuel price hike
summary: A sudden increase in fuel prices has pushed up transport and food costs, reversing a two-month decline in the inflation rate.
details: Point-to-point inflation in Bangladesh rose to 8.34 percent in September, according to updated data from the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS).
This increase reverses a two-month downward trend, as inflation had previously fallen to 8.32 percent in July and 8.26 percent in August.
The spike is attributed to a fuel price hike on September 20, where the government increased the prices of four types of fuel by Tk 20 per litre.
Zahid Hussain, a former lead economist at the World Bank’s Dhaka office, noted that the hike immediately pushed up transport and food costs.
The impact of these higher costs was reflected in commodity prices during the final 10 days of September.
Economists warn that the effect of the fuel price shock will likely continue, making it improbable for inflation to fall in the next one or two months.

Inflation is back on the rise. A fuel price hike has pushed the rate to 8.34% in September, hitting food and transport costs.

Point-to-point inflation in Bangladesh rose to 8.34 percent in September, according to updated data from the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS).

This increase reverses a two-month downward trend, as inflation had previously fallen to 8.32 percent in July and 8.26 percent in August.

The spike is attributed to a fuel price hike on September 20, where the government increased the prices of four types of fuel by Tk 20 per litre.

Zahid Hussain, a former lead economist at the World Bank’s Dhaka office, noted that the hike immediately pushed up transport and food costs.

The impact of these higher costs was reflected in commodity prices during the final 10 days of September.

Economists warn that the effect of the fuel price shock will likely continue, making it improbable for inflation to fall in the next one or two months.

topic: US loses 81 aircraft in Iran conflict
headline_marked: US loses [[81 aircraft and drones]] in conflict with Iran
headline: US loses 81 aircraft and drones in conflict with Iran
summary: A Congressional Research Service report estimates the losses at approximately $3.3 billion, including stealth fighters and Reaper drones.
details: The US military has lost or seen damaged at least 81 aircraft, unmanned drones, and helicopters over the last eight months of conflict with Iran, according to a Congressional Research Service (CRS) report.
The estimated market value of these losses is approximately $3.3 billion.
The losses include 12 F-15E Strike Eagle fighter jets, one F-35A Lightning II stealth fighter, and two A-10 Thunderbolt II attack aircraft.
At least 45 MQ-9 Reaper drones were lost, with each drone estimated to cost between $30 million and $50 million.
Specific incidents include the loss of three F-15E aircraft in a 'friendly fire' incident over Kuwait on March 2, and another destroyed during operations in Iranian airspace in April.
Eight more F-15E jets were slightly damaged during an Iranian attack on the Muwaffaq Salti airbase in Jordan in September.
An F-35A, one of the US's most advanced fighters valued at over $92 million, was damaged during an Iranian attack on March 19.

The US began military operations against Iran under 'Operation Epic Fury' on February 28, which was officially ended by Secretary of State Marco Rubio in early June. However, mutual attacks have continued in the following months.
caption:
81 aircraft and drones lost. $3.3 billion in damages. The cost of the US-Iran conflict is staggering.

The US military has lost or seen damaged at least 81 aircraft, unmanned drones, and helicopters over the last eight months of conflict with Iran, according to a Congressional Research Service (CRS) report.

The estimated market value of these losses is approximately $3.3 billion.

The losses include 12 F-15E Strike Eagle fighter jets, one F-35A Lightning II stealth fighter, and two A-10 Thunderbolt II attack aircraft.

At least 45 MQ-9 Reaper drones were lost, with each drone estimated to cost between $30 million and $50 million.

Specific incidents include the loss of three F-15E aircraft in a 'friendly fire' incident over Kuwait on March 2, and another destroyed during operations in Iranian airspace in April.

Eight more F-15E jets were slightly damaged during an Iranian attack on the Muwaffaq Salti airbase in Jordan in September.

An F-35A, one of the US's most advanced fighters valued at over $92 million, was damaged during an Iranian attack on March 19.

The US began military operations against Iran under 'Operation Epic Fury' on February 28, which was officially ended by Secretary of State Marco Rubio in early June. However, mutual attacks have continued in the following months.
